rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the land have been entrusted with leadership on condition that they fulfill its responsibilities.
rows.anchor: been given the leadership of the world on the condition that they give due importance to it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though many are ungrateful, sensible people lead in virtue and profess faith in the Qur’an; those who spurn God’s favor meet the fate prescribed for such rejecters.
rows.anchor: there are sensible and those among them who take lead in doing virtuous deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are successors to earlier nations, and God applies the same justice to them while their respite increases their loss.
rows.anchor: He has the same scale for all; He is giving respite to the Quraysh in spite of their rebelliousness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s respite is gracious, but when He seizes the Quraysh their alleged deities cannot help them; God alone holds the heavens and earth in place.
rows.anchor: The heavens and the earth remain at their place because of God; this is not because of deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh had vowed to become the world’s most guided people if a prophet came, but instead they conspire against him and invite the same wrath that befell earlier rejecters.
rows.anchor: they are busy day and night in conspiring against him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can stop God if He chooses to seize people immediately, though He sets a time for each nation’s judgment.
rows.anchor: He has appointed a time of His decision for each nation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s discourse has internal coherence and a relationship with the previous sūrah.
rows.anchor: portrays its internal coherence and its relationship with the previous sūrah

none: Qur’anic text and its translation only; no explanation yet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion rests on monotheism, whose foundation is gratitude, because God created the heavens and earth and bestowed every inward and outward favor.
rows.anchor: The foundation of religion rests on monotheism and the foundation of monotheism is gratitude

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of angels after the general reference to the Creator specifies that the same God created them as messengers.
rows.anchor: the specific after the general is that the God Who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth is the One Who has created angels as messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are singled out because Arab mythology made them especially important and treated them as God’s favored daughters, worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: Angels are specially mentioned because in Arab mythology they held the most importance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs thought angels could secure everything if pleased, making God merely ceremonial while idols named for angels became the focus of worship.
rows.anchor: the fountainhead of all their thanksgiving and worship would be their idols

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes angelic divinity: angels neither created the heavens and earth nor share divinity; they only convey God’s decrees to messengers.
rows.anchor: these angels neither have any share in the creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who assign divine power to envoys and worship them have failed to recognize God, His messengers, and their own status.
rows.anchor: Such people have neither recognized the status of God nor of His messengers nor of themselves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “possessing wings” describes the messengers, and ajniḥah is the plural of janaḥ, which can mean human arms or bird wings.
rows.anchor: The word يِولُأُ ٍةَحِن ْجَأُ is an attribute of ًلَاُسُر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since “wings” is mutashābihāt, only God knows their reality; the varied numbers indicate angels’ different ranks, forms, abilities, and potentials.
rows.anchor: Hence, it is of the nature of mutashābihāt: only God knows its reality

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two, three, and four wings indicate different angelic capacities and ranks, created according to divine expediency.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to inform us that not all angels are of the same status

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows the extent of angels’ flight, and listing four wings does not set a maximum; the verse only indicates different categories and ranks.
rows.anchor: this mention of four is not meant to mention a limit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narratives give Gabriel a greater number of wings, implying flight and access exceeding those of other angels.
rows.anchor: certain narratives mention a greater number of wings of Gabriel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These details rebuke those who deify angels: angels have different powers and capacities, let alone being God’s associates.
rows.anchor: The purpose of mentioning these details here is that the naïve who have accorded divinity to the angels

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels acknowledge assigned ranks, stand arrayed before God, and glorify Him, illustrating their subordinate status.
rows.anchor: We stand arrayed before God. And We glorify Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can create creatures with any strength or ability; the angels’ varied powers and their role as messengers manifest divine power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: God has the power to create creatures of any strength, potential and ability

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing or decreasing a creature’s capacities belongs to God and gives no creature a claim to divinity or partnership.
rows.anchor: No one has the authority to claim divinity on its basis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains why God alone deserves gratitude: no one can block blessings He opens or open what He withholds.
rows.anchor: Only God has this authority. Hence He alone is worthy of gratitude and worship

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 39:38 makes the same point: idols cannot avert harm or prevent a blessing if God wills it.
rows.anchor: these things which you worship could relieve my affliction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking angels or jinn as authorities over harm and benefit is foolish; only God has that authority and deserves worship and gratitude.
rows.anchor: Only God has this authority. Hence He alone is worthy of gratitude and worship

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same noun for mercy takes a feminine pronoun first and a masculine pronoun later, because the first refers to its form and the latter to its meaning.
rows.anchor: first a feminine pronoun is used and then a masculine one for the same noun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Min baʿdihi” means “after His withholding”; verse 35:41 uses the same idea when none can hold the heavens back after they fall.
rows.anchor: actually means نِم ِدْعَب ِاكَمسِإِِه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true sovereign: He opens and withholds according to the requirements of His wisdom.
rows.anchor: He opens and He stops and these acts are as per the requisites of His wisdom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arab idolaters themselves would acknowledge that God alone is creator and provider.
rows.anchor: would themselves give this very answer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to leave the rejecters to the fate of their predecessors.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should leave them alone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh mock the threatened doom, but when God’s promise arrives they will see it before them.
rows.anchor: why and from where will the promised doom come upon them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone provides, the address asks why people have lost their senses and turned to other deities.
rows.anchor: why have they lost their senses and made up other deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not grieve at rejection: earlier messengers were also denied, and these rejecters will follow their predecessors’ fate.
rows.anchor: Such people have denied messengers before him as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All matters are and will be presented to God, who will issue the final verdict; the Prophet should trust Him and leave the rejecters’ fate to Him.
rows.anchor: everything is coming before Him and will come in the future as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are warned that God’s promised judgment is real; worldly wealth does not prove they are rightly guided or disprove the threatened doom.
rows.anchor: The affluence they possess in this world should not deceive them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-gharūr means “the deceiver” and refers here to Satan.
rows.anchor: The word ُورُرَغْال means “the deceiver” and here it denotes Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is the greatest deceiver and misleads people about God’s attributes; respite does not mean they are beyond God’s grasp or protected by idols.
rows.anchor: Satan, the deceiver should not deceive them in the matter of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is merciful yet severe in retribution; He has no partner, and no one can stop Him from seizing anyone.
rows.anchor: Neither does God have a partner nor can anyone stop Him from seizing anyone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misleading people begins by distorting their understanding of God’s attributes, as Qur’an 82:6 warns.
rows.anchor: the basis of all luring away from the truth is that which relates to God’s attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is an inveterate enemy, so people must guard against him instead of treating their foe as chief and leader.
rows.anchor: people must consider an enemy as enemy and be on guard from his moves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s sole aim in calling his followers is to lead them into Hell.
rows.anchor: his sole purpose is to lead them to the pit of Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 7 explains God’s inevitable promise: the world will not continue without a final distinction between evil and good.
rows.anchor: this world will continue on with its journey without any distinction being made between vice and virtue

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who assume vice and virtue will remain indistinguishable have been deceived about God’s attributes; a day of judgment will bring punishment to disbelievers and reward to righteous believers.
rows.anchor: A day is bound to come wherein the disbelievers will face a grievous doom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not blame himself for their disbelief; their moral blindness follows God’s established practice, and God knows and will judge their deeds.
rows.anchor: if these people are not professing faith, then this is not because of any fault of his

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause’s answer is suppressed; expanded, it asks whether one whose evil seems good can be guided, implying such people do not receive guidance.
rows.anchor: whose evil deeds have been made fair to him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 39:19 restates the point by asking whether one can rescue a person already deserving punishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: He who has become worthy of punishment, will then you be able to rescue him who is in Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner who feels remorse may reform when warned, while someone who regards foul deeds as talent, progress, culture, and education shows corruption of heart and intellect.
rows.anchor: In the first state one can expect a person to correct himself if he is reminded and warned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls this hardened condition heart-sealing or rust; one afflicted by it cannot be guided.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ān calls such a state as khatm-i qulūb (heart-sealing) or rayn (rust)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words about God leading astray and guiding point to His established practice, which the sūrah explains further later.
rows.anchor: point to the established practice of God prescribed by him about providing guidance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse tells the Prophet not to fret over those whose deeds seem good to them.
rows.anchor: So do not fret yourself in their grief

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ḥasarāt can be parsed as an accusative of state or of cause; both constructions occur in classical Arabic.
rows.anchor: can grammatically be an accusative of state or an accusative of cause

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the author’s opinion, “ʿalayhim” is connected to ḥasarāt, as in Qur’an 30:36.
rows.anchor: in my opinion, is related to ٍاتَرَسَح the way it is in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ḥasarāt intensifies the depth of sorrow.
rows.anchor: The plurality of the word ٍاتَرَسَح expresses profundity of sorrow

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who denied God’s Book at the time of revelation likewise deserve the punishment already described, connecting the discourse to its original setting.
rows.anchor: This statement has linked the discourse to the situation that existed at the time of its revelation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hell, the condemned plead for release so they can return to the world and act differently from before.
rows.anchor: they will plead to God to grant them respite so that they could go back in the previous world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that they had enough life to heed the reminder and a warner came; they receive no further support and must taste their deserved punishment.
rows.anchor: were they not granted enough respite which was sufficient for them to pay heed to God’s reminder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given sufficient lifespan and a warner who conclusively communicates truth receive no concession; people who die before maturity are treated more leniently.
rows.anchor: those whom the Almighty has given enough life span and the truth has also been conclusively communicated to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the unseen of heaven and earth, so His warnings will come to pass; He also knows that people asking for respite would repeat their old conduct.
rows.anchor: if these people are given this chance they will again do what they used to do

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs are warned that they succeed earlier nations destroyed for rejecting messengers; God’s law is uniform, and their deities do not sustain the heavens or earth.
rows.anchor: they are in fact the successors of the previous nations: so they should seek a lesson

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nations more powerful than Quraysh were destroyed for rejecting their messengers, so Quraysh should learn from their fate.
rows.anchor: If these nations, in spite of being more powerful than them were destroyed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs are urged to take a lesson from earlier nations’ circumstances and fate.
rows.anchor: so they should seek a lesson from their circumstances and the fate they met

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God releases His hold on the heavens and earth, none but He can keep them together; Arab deities have no such power.
rows.anchor: If God let goes of them no one else can hold them together

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s arrogant opposition and conspiracies followed their earlier boast that they would lead the nations in guidance if a messenger arrived.
rows.anchor: when the messenger actually came, out of sheer arrogance, they set about to oppose him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final section’s changed verse-rhymes signal a change in speaker tone and direct attention to a new aspect.
rows.anchor: This sudden change in intonation points to the change in the tone and pitch of the speaker

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s political leadership in Arabia is neither their own achievement nor unprecedented; earlier arrogant disbelieving nations were destroyed, and they have succeeded those nations.
rows.anchor: the political leadership they enjoy in the land of Arabia is neither because of their own effort nor are they the first ones to acquire it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s standard for the rise and fall of nations is impartial; the Quraysh will repeat the history of the nations whose accounts they heard.
rows.anchor: God’s barometer of justice regarding the rise and fall of nations is unflinching and unbiased

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Quraysh imitate earlier nations’ arrogance and disbelief, they should expect the same fate.
rows.anchor: if they too adopt the same attitude as these nations, then they should be prepared to meet the same fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse exposes the baselessness of the deities invoked beside God and asks whether they created anything or share in governing the heavens.
rows.anchor: if these deities have created anything in the heavens and the earth, then they should show it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Raʾaytum” in this rhetorical setting conveys amazement and disgust.
rows.anchor: on such occasions signifies amazement and disgust

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from direct to indirect address intensifies the earlier amazement and disgust while asking whether God gave them a scripture authorizing partners.
rows.anchor: the style of address has shifted from direct to indirect; this has increased the amazement and disgust

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question implies that their deities have neither a role in creation nor any divine authorization to be partners.
rows.anchor: Has God given them a book in which He has pointed out His partners

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With no argument or sanction, wrongdoers mislead one another through leaders’ false claims about idols’ powers and promised blessings.
rows.anchor: such people who wrong their souls are misleading one another without any argument or sanction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people expect their deities to protect them, they should remember that God alone keeps the heavens and earth in their orbits; if He loosens their reins, the whole system collapses.
rows.anchor: If He loosens their reins, no one has the power to hold them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s respite despite human arrogance reflects His graciousness and mercy: He is not hasty and gives people time to mend their ways.
rows.anchor: He does not show haste in punishing them He ignores them and gives them respite

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabia’s unlettered people were regarded by Jews as inferior; Jewish jurists permitted taking entrusted wealth from them and charging them interest.
rows.anchor: their jurists had issued an edict that usurping the wealth placed in the trust of the unlettered

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to Jewish disparagement, the Arab idolaters swore that if a messenger came they would be more guided than other nations.
rows.anchor: these Idolaters would on oath arrogantly swear before them that if ever a messenger is sent to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures predict the final messenger among the Ishmaelites; Jewish scholars concealed the predictions, while some Christians awaited an Arab messenger.
rows.anchor: the predictions found in the previous scriptures regarding the advent of the last messenger clearly state that he will come in the Ishmaelites

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Christians awaited an Arab messenger, and Qur’an 5:83 describes People of Scripture moved to tears by recognizing the revelation’s truth.
rows.anchor: you see their eyes shed tears because of recognizing the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ishmaelites had a tradition that a messenger would come to them and claimed they would accept his guidance more readily than the Jews; his coming instead increased their aversion.
rows.anchor: they will not prove meek and weak like the Jews and in fact take lead in accepting his guidance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah Ṣāffāt recalls their claim that they would be God’s chosen servants if they had earlier teaching, followed by their rejection and warning of consequences.
rows.anchor: Had we any teaching of the earlier generations we would have been among God’s chosen servants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance explains their aversion: although the truth is clear, they fear losing their authority and leadership if they accept Muḥammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: The truth is fully evident to them; yet they are not willing to sacrifice at any cost the position of authority and leadership they hold

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “evil scheme” is coordinated grammatically with “aversion.”
rows.anchor: are co-ordinated to  اًورُفُن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil plotting rebounds on its author, and God’s established practice for earlier peoples cannot be changed or stopped.
rows.anchor: you will neither find any change in the established practice of God nor will you find it to cease
